why: IMAGE-SCRIPT-MATCH-1: the os-release ID each marketplace image runs, so ImageScriptMatch.Tests.ps1 can prove that every image data/supported-images.json admits has a branch in each guest script that switches on the distribution. The offers are the names Azure listed (az vm image list-offers, read only). The IDs are the os-release ID field of each distribution, with the source of each in ids. An image whose ID nobody measured has osReleaseId null and names the item that measures it (gap); its test is skipped with that item, never passed.
offersRead: az vm image list-offers -l centralus, 2026-11-14, publishers Canonical, RedHat, SUSE, Debian, Oracle, MicrosoftCBLMariner, microsoft-dsvm, MicrosoftSQLServer

ids.ubuntu: data/driver-floors.json: Microsoft's MANA table names Ubuntu by this os-release ID. The VM agent reports ubuntu (measured 2026-10-11, ConvertTo-VmfDistroId).
ids.rhel: data/driver-floors.json: Microsoft's MANA table names Red Hat Enterprise Linux by this os-release ID.
ids.sles: data/driver-floors.json: Microsoft's MANA table names SUSE Linux Enterprise Server by this os-release ID. The VM agent reports sles (measured 2026-10-11).
ids.sles_sap: src/guest/linux/kernel-update.sh names sles_sap as the os-release ID of SUSE Linux Enterprise Server for SAP Applications. The scan refuses SAP images (Test-VmfSapImage).
ids.debian: data/driver-floors.json: Microsoft's MANA table names Debian by this os-release ID. The VM agent reports debian (measured 2026-10-11).
ids.ol: data/driver-floors.json: Microsoft's MANA table names Oracle Linux by this os-release ID.
ids.azurelinux: data/driver-floors.json: Microsoft's MANA table names Azure Linux 3 and 4 by this os-release ID.
ids.mariner: src/guest/linux/kernel-update.sh names mariner as the os-release ID of CBL-Mariner (Azure Linux 2.0).
ids.opensuse-leap: src/guest/linux/kernel-update.sh names opensuse-leap as the os-release ID of openSUSE Leap.
ids.centos: src/guest/linux/nvme-fix.sh and kernel-update.sh name centos as the os-release ID of CentOS.
